messages:
meera: Heads-up — we just saw an unexpected daytime surge across us-central and eu-west. Tokens/sec jumped ~3x for a 20-minute window and tail latency spiked. GPUs are reporting high KV-cache churn. Can infra triage headroom and quick mitigations?

alex: seeing it on dashboards. aggregate tokens/s 5m avg went from 220k -> 680k. concurrent live requests climbed from ~4.2k to ~11.8k. GPU util on p4p pools hit 92% for a sustained 6m.

jordan: thanks. running quick query: `sum(rate(redwood_requests_tokens_total[5m]))` returns ~680k tokens/s. per-GPU steady throughput estimate ~30k tokens/s (with current batching config). that implies ~23 GPUs worth of load instead of 8.

meera: rough headroom math — we only had ~2.5% spare in the auto-scaling window because autoscale target is conservative during business hours. need quick options: burst to reserved, spin new spot pool, or degrade to smaller model variants. cost vs risk?

sasha: we can enable burst-capacity (reserved-pool fallback) now — requires toggle and 5m warm-up. alternative: enable model-fallback to quantized-v2 for non-enterprise traffic (should preserve correctness for most calls).

ops-bot: Incident note: `daytime-thin-spike-1956789012` created. Paging on-call if unchanged after 10m.

alex: short-term plan: 1) enable reserved burst (scale +12 GPUs) 2) raise autoscale ceiling by 30% for 1h 3) flip fallback route for non-SLA routes to quantized-v2. Doing 1 now.

jordan: running a quick cost calc: +12 A100 equiv for 1 hour ~ $X/hr * 12 -> ~ $Y one-off. If this is recurring daily peak we need ~200 GPU-hours/week which is material.

meera: note on root cause candidates: 1) marketing campaign driving heavy chat summarize jobs 2) cache hit-rate regressions (KV eviction increased) 3) cross-region reroutes earlier causing hot shards. logs show increased prefix cache misses.

alex: log excerpt: ```
[2026-07-14T18:12:03Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction_rate=0.27 miss_rate=0.42 pool=p4p-us-central shard=7
[2026-07-14T18:12:07Z] INFO serve: inflight_requests=11750 avg_latency_ms=360
```

sasha: I pushed a config to bump per-worker cache size by 10% in the us-central pool — should reduce eviction for short-window contexts. rolling patch in 2m.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaling us-central/p4p +12 GPUs (requested). expected ready ~5m.

jordan: after burst: tokens/s back to ~260k and concurrent ~5.1k. GPUs down to 68% util. tail p99 latency dropped from 720ms -> 220ms. looks effective for now.

meera: follow-ups: - add a weekly simulation for daytime marketing spike (model tokens/sec distribution, concurrency) - revisit autoscale policy: allow short 15m burst headroom for known campaign windows - add alert for cache miss rate >0.2 on any pool (currently only total latency alert) - estimate reserved capacity needs if this repeats (how many guaranteed GPUs to buy/commit).

alex: I'll run a quick throughput-to-GPU model: assume median request length 120 tokens, avg tokens/sec per GPU 30k, concurrency mapping will vary with seq len. I'll push a small spreadsheet.

sasha: also flag network egress spikiness — eu-west reported increased retransmits during the spike window; could be making some requests slower and keeping slots occupied longer. ops will review peering metrics.

meera: for the docops/finance ask: Jordan/ Alex — can you give a 30-day projection if marketing traffic doubles 4x for 3 hours/day? want GPU-hours delta and ballpark monthly cost to present to finance.

jordan: on it. preliminary: doubling to 4x for 3h/day => ~+600 GPU-hours/month at current mix. I'll break out hosted vs dedicated exposure.

ops-bot: Incident update: resolved via reserved burst + cache bump. Monitoring for 30m.

meera: good job. logging action items here: `#todo` 1) simulation + spreadsheet from Alex/Jordan 2) autoscale tweak (15m burst window) 3) cache miss alert + investigate eviction pattern 4) network peering check for eu-west 5) cost option (reserved vs temporary burst)

alex: posted spreadsheet link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/infra/1956789012-capacity-scan (contains throughput model, tokens->GPUs mapping, cost scenarios).

jordan: will follow up with finance numbers by EOD.

meera: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes and add to weekly capacity sync.
